newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-PRIME MINISTER MAJOR MEETS FA TO DISCUSS WORLD CUP BID.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-PRIME MINISTER MAJOR MEETS FA TO DISCUSS WORLD CUP BID.

text.p: Prime Minister John Major is to meet England soccer coach Glenn Hoddle and Football Association (FA) officials on Monday to discuss a possible bid to stage the World Cup in 2006, an aide to Major said.

He said the FA had very clear ideas to be outlined to Major, a keen soccer fan and supporter of London's Chelsea club, about how to build on the success of the Euro 96 tournament staged in England in June.
Monday's meeting is scheduled for 1700 gmt at Major's Downing Street office. FA chief executive Graham Kelly and spokesman David Davies will attend with Hoddle.
The aide noted that 2006 would mark the 40th anniversary of England's last hosting of the World Cup, when the home side defeated Germany in the final at London's Wembley Stadium.

National Heritage Secretary Virginia Bottomley said in June the government would back the FA all the way if it decided to offer to stage the World Cup, hinting that money could be made available from Britain's national lottery.
